attribution.note: Marcus's own words, in his own list of 2026 predictions.

semantics.note: A firm 'will' forecast, horizon the 2026 midterms. The normalisation is faithful.

contract.note: The contract counts any substantive campaign commitment as an 'election issue'. On that reading, a two-sentence 2024 platform plank defeats 'first time'. An informed reader would take 'election issue' to mean a salient campaign topic that follows from the backlash Marcus describes, not a minor platform line. That reading is stretched against the speaker. Also, Election Day (Nov 3) falls after the evaluation date.

evidence.note: Real 2024 GOP platform plank pledging to repeal Biden's AI executive order. Correctly dated. It is a brief mention and does not show AI was a salient election issue in 2024, so it does not contradict 'first time' on a fair reading.
An advocacy group's own announcement that 18 candidates signed an AI pledge. Partial, self-reported sign that AI is a 2026 campaign subject. It says nothing about salience or novelty.

reviews.rationale: The midterm campaign runs through Nov 3, 2026, after the evaluation date. The early-resolution rule depends on an unfair reading under which a minor 2024 platform plank makes AI an earlier 'election issue'. On a fair reading, the novelty claim is not defeated. e2 shows some 2026 campaign activity on AI, but the outcome is not yet settled.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words, in his list of 2026 predictions.

semantics.note: A firm 'will' forecast. Taking the horizon as calendar 2026 matches the framing as predictions for 2026.

contract.note: The plain reading (no country clearly and durably ahead on frontier model capability) is ordinary and fair. 'Decisive' has no stated threshold.

evidence.note: News report of the Stanford 2026 AI Index. As of March 2026, top US and Chinese models were close and had traded the lead. Consistent with the forecast, but a mid-year snapshot, not the year-end state.

reviews.rationale: The forecast window runs to 2026-12-31, after the evaluation date. No early-resolution event (a large, sustained gap judged decisive) appears in the packet. The March 2026 data show a narrow gap, consistent with the forecast, but the forecast cannot be scored before its deadline.
